prompt.startup_instruction:
Before generating any code, first consult my Taste MCP and design front-end skills context on front end design. Use those references to guide all interface design, layout hierarchy, spacing, typography, interaction polish, and visual decision-making.
The interface should feel thoughtfully designed, modern, minimal, and educationally approachable for middle school students.
Prioritize excellent front-end craftsmanship over feature bloat.
prompt.project:
Build a browser-based SVG vector editor called "Laser Maker" for middle school students creating designs for laser cutting machines.
The application should feel like a simplified Adobe Illustrator built specifically for children and rapid prototyping.

core_workspace.feature: Artboard size can be set by user in real-world inches (example: 12x12, 18x24, 24x36)
Horizontal and vertical rulers on workspace edges similar to Adobe Illustrator
Button to reset zoom to true 1:1 physical scale where on-screen inches match real design inches as accurately as browser/device allows

tools.tool: Bézier pen tool behaving similarly to Adobe Illustrator: click to place anchors, drag for handles, edit curves cleanly

path_operations.feature: Shape-builder style interaction if practical, otherwise keep simple pathfinder buttons

export.feature: Export clean SVG to size of canvas board
Preserve physical sizing for laser cutting workflows

design_requirements.ui: Clear, modern interface that is on brand for NYC FIRST
Similar layout conventions to Illustrator but dramatically simplified

important_constraints.constraint: Do NOT attempt full Illustrator complexity
Relying on less external libraries is better. Make decisions on what implementation to leverage in order to achieve the goal.
Keep first prototype simple and highly functional
Build only enough to establish strong foundation
